real_s2.explanation: The unit responds to furry mammal heads, mostly dogs, seen frontally at a moderate scale (head and upper body filling roughly a quarter to half of the image), with the neck/shoulder region beside the face and furry ears clearly visible. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals with similar head structure.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to furry mammal heads, mostly dogs, seen frontally at a moderate scale (head and upper body filling roughly a quarter to half of the image), with the neck/shoulder region beside the face and furry ears clearly visible. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals with similar head structure.
parsed.evidence: The top classes are almost all dog breeds plus meerkat and wolf, and within classes activity is strongly higher when the neck/shoulder area is clearly visible (d +0.62, 99th percentile), the head and upper body fill a quarter to half of the image (d +0.75, 98th percentile), and the head is frontal with furry ears visible. Fur length itself does not separate the photos (6th percentile), and a left-facing or right-of-center subject lowers activity.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on non-dog furry mammals and on non-mammal images with similar framing would show how far the response extends beyond dogs, and spatial activation maps would confirm whether the response sits on the neck/shoulder region.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to the head and fore-body of furry mammals, mostly dogs, and is most active when the head faces the camera, is sharp and well lit, and has the furry neck/shoulder area beside the face clearly in view, with the head-and-upper-body filling a quarter to half of the frame. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to the head and fore-body of furry mammals, mostly dogs, and is most active when the head faces the camera, is sharp and well lit, and has the furry neck/shoulder area beside the face clearly in view, with the head-and-upper-body filling a quarter to half of the frame. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals.
parsed.evidence: Within its top classes, the strongest and most unusual separators are neck/shoulder visibility (clearly visible d +0.62 vs partly visible d -0.68, 99th percentile) and medium framing of head and upper body (d +0.75, 98th percentile), backed by a prominent frontal head with visible furry ears. Fur length does not separate photos at all (6th percentile), and dog versus other mammal barely matters, so fur amount is not what drives the unit within these classes.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on non-mammal or synthetic images that show a head-plus-neck layout without fur, and on mammal crops of the neck only versus the face only, to check whether the unit needs fur or just this head-and-shoulders arrangement. It would also help to know why the unrelated 'lab coat' class ranks among its top classes.
